interest: Japan's 1940 civil service changes and personnel exchanges with its puppet regimes.
overview: This file consists of a single State Department despatch (No. 4767) dated June 11, 1940, from U.S. Ambassador to Japan Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo to the Secretary of State in Washington, reporting on five proposed major revisions to Japan's civil service system under deliberation by the Cabinet and the Cabinet Committee for the Improvement of the Civil Service. The proposed measures include consolidating administrative and diplomatic civil service entrance examinations while eliminating compulsory foreign language testing; abolishing the 1932 ordinance protecting civil servants' personal status and tenure in an effort to curb bureaucratic entrenchment; granting bonuses and considering wartime allowances for lower-level officials despite wage-freeze legislation; authorizing the appointment of private sector experts to high-ranking Chokunin policy and administrative posts; and granting full civil service rank and salary equivalence to Japanese officials returning from service in Manchukuo, the reorganized Nanking Government, and provisional regimes in North China and Mongolia.

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting on five major proposals being considered by the Japanese Cabinet to reform the civil service system, examinations, tenure protections, remuneration, private expert appointments, and overseas service credit.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew outlines five key civil service reform measures under consideration by the Japanese Cabinet and its Committee for the Improvement of the Civil Service. These include merging administrative and diplomatic civil service examinations and eliminating required foreign language tests despite Foreign Ministry objections, as well as abolishing the 1932 ordinance protecting bureaucratic tenure to address growing complaints of bureaucratic arrogance. The reforms also address early bonus distribution and wartime allowances for lower-level officials, the recruitment of private-sector specialists into Chokunin-rank policymaking and bureau directorship roles, and the granting of full civil service seniority to Japanese officials returning from service in Manchukuo and puppet regimes in China.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4767 from Joseph C. Grew on Proposed Changes in the Japanese Civil Service
